plainLanguage: Different parts of the chest muscle do measurably different amounts of work, and which part works hardest depends on the movement.
qualifiers: The phenomenon is reported by five independent method families; the magnitudes are not comparable across them and are not pooled.
Individual samples are small, between eight and forty-eight participants or specimens.
The strongest regional activation evidence is from female participants only, while most of the exercise activation evidence is from male participants only.
Regional differentiation in activation is not by itself evidence that a region can be grown selectively by training.

conditions: isometric and ballistic shoulder tasks, passive stretch, and cadaveric moment-arm measurement
scope.population: healthy adults and adult cadaveric specimens

statement: The regions of the pectoralis major are not activated or loaded as one unit: measured moment arms, regional electromyography and tissue-stiffness measurement each show that its sub-regions differ from one another.
